subject: Data residency & default retention — EU prospect questions
messages:
From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@finevo.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@finevo.com
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Quick clarifications — what do you keep by default (EU)?

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for speaking with our procurement team last week. Before we proceed to the legal review, our InfoSec folks asked for a short, plain-language summary of Redwood's default data capture and retention for EU customers. In particular they want to confirm the following items so we can map them to our policy gap analysis:

- Which artifacts are stored by default in hosted accounts created in the EU region: raw prompts/requests, model outputs, streaming fragments, KV cache contents, embeddings, and telemetry?
- Default retention periods for each of the above (if different).
- Do backups or snapshots contain customer request data beyond the stated retention window?
- Can data be pinned to EU-only storage? If we sign a contract, can we require all copies (backups, logs, monitoring) to remain within the EU?
- What is the erasure process and evidence we will receive once a deletion request is completed?

If you can send a one-page summary plus any supporting artifacts (matrix or SOC2 snippet) that would be ideal. We may loop in our legal/security for a short call.

Appreciate it —
Anna
Anna Ruiz
Senior Security Manager, FineEvo Bank

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@finevo.com>
Cc: compliance@finevo.com
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications — what do you keep by default (EU)?

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary aimed at InfoSec/legal. I kept it high level; happy to follow up with a short call and the retention matrix attached.

Summary (hosted accounts created in the EU region / default settings):

- Prompts / Requests (user inputs): Retained by default for 30 days. These are used for operational debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring. Customers can enable an opt-out flag at account level to disable storing request payloads.

- Model Outputs (final responses): Not persisted long-term by default. For standard hosted usage, the final model outputs are transient and are kept only to serve the immediate API response; a short-lived cache (to support retries/streams) is held for up to 6 hours and then evicted. Outputs are persisted only if the customer explicitly enables archival/storage features (examples: indexing, vector stores, or explicit 'store_responses' flag).

- Streaming Fragments / Token Buffers: Held in-memory during the session/stream. If a session completes successfully, fragments are folded into the ephemeral response cache (see previous) and removed within 6 hours. If a session is aborted, fragments are not written to persistent logs.

- KV Cache (serving runtime internal state): Ephemeral; by default TTL is 24 hours and it is never written to durable backups outside runtime unless a customer chooses a workflow that materializes caches for debugging (rare, opt-in).

- Embeddings / Indexes: Created embeddings or indexes are customer-controlled: we store them only when customers write them to their project storage (e.g., for search/indexing). If created via the API but not persisted by the customer, they are treated like derived outputs and follow the storage/opt-in rules above.

- Telemetry / Aggregated Logs: Non-identifying telemetry (performance metrics, aggregate latencies) is retained for 90 days by default for product operations and trend analysis. Any logs that contain identifiers are treated under the request/response retention windows above.

Backups / Snapshots: Our standard backup cadence in the hosted EU region keeps redundant snapshots for up to 7 days for disaster recovery. Backups do not extend primary retention windows for customer request data: when a deletion is requested, we also schedule removal from backups per the restore-safety window (see erasure below). If you require longer backup isolation inside the EU, we can discuss contractual terms or Private/Dedicated deployment models.

Data Residency Options:
- By default, accounts created in EU regions have their data stored in EU data centers.
- For contractual guarantees (all copies, logs, backups pinned to EU), we offer Dedicated and Private deployment options with EU-only commitments and customer-managed keys.

Erasure / Evidence:
- Standard erasure path: submit a deletion request via Support (we can provide a template). We mark the data for deletion immediately and run a multi-stage purge: remove from live indexes, remove durable stores, then trigger background reclaim for backups/bins.
- Evidence provided: deletion job ID, timestamped audit record (what keys/objects removed), and a confirmation email when reclaim completes. Audit records for deletion jobs are kept for 365 days for audit reasons but contain pointers (job ids, object ids) rather than customer payloads.

Attachments: SOC2 excerpt and a condensed retention matrix attached below.

Next steps: happy to join a 30–40 minute call with your security/legal to walk through this matrix and any contract language. If you want more granular SLAs (e.g., 14-day backup purge), we can escalate to Sales/Legal as part of a Dedicated/Private proposal.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Trust & Safety (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf (stub), retention-matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@finevo.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: FineEvo Compliance <compliance@finevo.com>, legal@finevo.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 08:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications — what do you keep by default (EU)?

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team:

- During the deletion window (the 7-day backup window you mentioned), is there a risk that deleted request data could be restored via a DR restore? If so, can we get a policy statement that deletion requests are prioritized and restores exclude purged objects?
- For the audit evidence: will the deletion job ID map to object identifiers we can reconcile on our side, or are they opaque? We need reconcilable identifiers for our retention attestation.
- Is customer-managed KMS available for hosted EU accounts or only for Private/Dedicated?

If you can loop in someone from your technical ops who can confirm backup/restore behavior and a legal contact for contractual language, that would be helpful.

Appreciate it —
Anna

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@finevo.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, compliance@finevo.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications — what do you keep by default (EU)?

Anna —

Looping in Kimberly (Security & Compliance) and Marissa (Product Ops) to supply the technical/contractual assurances you requested. Short answers up front, details below.

- Backup restores & deleted objects: Our restore process excludes objects that have been marked for deletion and passed their purge window. Operationally, when a deletion request is executed we set a deletion tombstone and remove the primary object; the backup restore tool honors these tombstones and will not reinstate purged objects during routine DR restores. For emergency recoveries we do have a small risk window where manual intervention may be required — in those cases we only restore after explicit confirmation and we maintain a restore-exclusion list. We can add contractual language prioritizing deletion exclusion for FineEvo.

- Deletion job IDs / reconciliation: Deletion job IDs map to internal object identifiers (stable keys) and we can provide a reconciliation report that contains object keys and timestamps (redacted where necessary) so FineEvo can match deletions to your local records. The reconciliation report is delivered as a signed artifact.

- Customer-managed keys (KMS): Customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest are available for Dedicated and Private deployments today. For hosted accounts we offer provider-managed keys by default; we can discuss a hosted KMS option under an enterprise addendum, but it is not standard on self-serve hosted accounts.

Technical clarifications from Marissa / Ops:
- Default retention table (for quick reference):
  * Requests / Prompts: 30 days (opt-out available at account level)
  * Final Outputs: transient; cache up to 6 hours unless customer enables storage
  * Streaming fragments: in-memory; persisted only to short cache (6 hours) on success
  * KV cache: TTL 24 hours by default; not in backups unless explicitly materialized
  * Embeddings: stored only if customer writes/persists them to project storage
  * Telemetry: aggregated 90 days
  * Backups: redundant snapshots kept up to 7 days

- Backup purge timeline: after a deletion runs, purge markers are propagated to backup systems within 48 hours; final reclaim from immutable backup tiers completed within 7 days. We can tighten these windows for contract commitments.

- Audit evidence retention: We retain deletion audit records (job id, affected object keys, timestamps, operator id) for 365 days to support attestation requests. The audit record does not contain payload data.

Next steps / Offer:
- I can attach a short machine-readable retention CSV if that helps automation (attached).
- Kimberly is available to review contractual language for an EU-only storage carve-out; we can propose language that explicitly enumerates backups and monitoring artifacts.
- We recommend a 30–40 minute call so we can finalize any SLAs and KMS options before legal drafts — Kimberly, Marissa: could you both join a call with FineEvo early next week?

Thanks —
Soojin
Head of Trust & Safety (EMEA)
Redwood Inference
